correctness.rationale: For t=0, a first forced vertex requires two colours across its full neighbourhood, leaving the initially incomplete opposite side unforceable, so a whole n-side must be seeded. For t>0, 0-2 seeds cannot finish; from any successful 3 seeds the two different colours on one side compel the third seed on the other side to repeat one colour, and properness forces the repeated colour across a deleted matched nonedge. The converse forces all but two opposite-side vertices, then remaining near-side vertices, then the last opposite-side vertex; n>=4 ensures available witnesses. Count t*3*2*2*(n-1)=12t(n-1). Package-local exhaustive checks over n=4..7,t>=1 and intact n=4..6 agree; no finite-to-infinite inference.

value.rationale: A one-edge perturbation of the dense regular bipartite graph changes the smallest successful three-colour seed set from n to 3 for arbitrary n>=4, exposing a nonlocal sharp instability of the recently introduced forcing polynomial. The theorem additionally classifies every minimum forcing assignment and gives the exact coefficient 12t(n-1) over the entire matching-deletion family, a structural prediction not supplied by the intact-biclique or degree-two results.
